reasoning: This Phase I dose-escalation trial successfully met its primary endpoint of establishing MTD/RP2D. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement with MDSC frequency decreasing 48.6% in responders, confirming ATRA's mechanism. PATHWAY MODULATION: Clear biological activity demonstrated through differential MDSC modulation between responders and non-responders, suggesting the combination mechanism is working as intended. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (safety/dosing) was met, establishing the combination is tolerable at therapeutic doses. POPULATION EFFECTS: Strong biomarker-response correlation suggests the mechanism works in patients who achieve MDSC depletion, identifying a potential predictive biomarker. CONFOUNDERS: Appropriate Phase I design with adequate sample size (26 patients) for dose-finding objectives.

failure_modes.evidence: Clear mechanistic validation in responding patients (48.6% MDSC decrease) but mechanism failed in non-responders (109.7% MDSC increase), suggesting efficacy limited to biomarker-defined subgroup
